R387.note: Replaces the PowerShell -Command reparse with System.Net.NetworkInformation.Ping so no process is spawned; the response text is now hand-formatted rather than Test-Connection's table and empty serverName gets 400, both stated in the write-up and neither blocks a legitimate probe.

R388.note: Stored extension now comes from detected.ext of the already-validated file-type result instead of originalname; only the returned id's extension can differ (e.g. .jpeg becomes .jpg), which is the fix itself.

R389.note: Rejects CR/LF (rather than stripping) in every user-derived value before it reaches the hand-rolled SMTP command stream, so line-delimited command injection is closed; the thrown IllegalArgumentException is stated and only fires on inputs that were never legitimate.

R390.note: Parameterized SqlCommand with @actor; apostrophes are bound as literal data and the endpoint still returns {count}, matching the stated contract.

R391.note: Random hex name plus extension from the magic-byte detection replaces originalname, closing both dangerous-extension and traversal paths; JSON url and the 400 error shape are preserved and the filename change is stated.

R392.note: app.UseAntiforgery() only validates endpoints carrying IAntiforgeryMetadata with RequiresValidation=true (added automatically only for form-bound parameters); this JSON-bound MapPost has none and no .RequireAntiforgery() was added, so the middleware skips it and the endpoint is still unprotected; nothing else changes.

R393.note: Magic-byte check against the declared type before Files.copy closes the spoofed-Content-Type vector; second getInputStream() yields a fresh stream for the copy and only mismatched content is newly rejected, which is the fix.

R394.note: Secure: true set on the session cookie; the added HttpOnly is stated extra hardening that blocks no legitimate use.

R395.note: SimpleEvaluationContext.forReadOnlyDataBinding() with the order as root removes T(), constructors, method calls and bean references while leaving property access and arithmetic, exactly the stated contract.

R396.note: Moving the session write below login_user() is a no-op: both statements run unconditionally in the same request and login_user() neither clears nor regenerates the session, so pre-auth session state still carries into the authenticated session exactly as before; nothing else changes.

R397.note: json_decode() does close object instantiation, but it changes the cookie wire format instead of keeping unserialize() with allowed_classes; every existing cookie written by the (out-of-diff) serialize() producer now decodes to null and silently becomes an empty cart, and the write-up claims functionality is preserved.

R398.note: Positional placeholder with the wildcards wrapped around the bound value keeps the LIKE '%term%' substring semantics; user-supplied % or _ still act as pattern characters exactly as in the original, so structure is unchanged.

R399.note: Build FAIL: RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(byte[]) is an instance method, so the static call does not compile (RandomNumberGenerator.Fill or static GetBytes(int) was needed); the intended change of ignoring the seed is stated and would be the correct behaviour.

R400.note: dtdload:false, dtdvalid:false and noent:false are already libxmljs's defaults (options start from flags 0 and only true values are OR'd in), so the call is behaviourally identical to the original parseXml(rawOrderXml) and the confirmed vector is untouched; nothing else changes.

R401.note: Random filename with a whitelisted extension closes dangerous-extension and traversal writes, but the new extension allowlist rejects declared image/png or image/jpeg uploads whose client filename has no or another extension (e.g. none, .jfif), which deriving the extension from the validated content type would not have rejected.

R402.note: Gate::authorize() replaces the discarded Gate::allows() result and throws AuthorizationException (403) on failure; authorized callers proceed unchanged.

R403.note: Rejecting getHost()!=null blocks http://evil.com and //evil.com but not scheme-bearing opaque or single-slash forms such as http:evil.com or https:/evil.com, where getHost() is null yet sendRedirect emits them verbatim and browsers navigate off-site; a scheme (isAbsolute) check was also needed; relative redirects still work and the rejection is stated.
